# C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage

*Level 1 card. 7 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption. This includes creating more objects than needed (unnecessary creation), copying data when in-place operations or references suffice (unnecessary copying), materializing lazy sequences into full collections prematurely (unnecessary materialization), retaining oversized structures when compact representations would work (oversized retaining), pre-allocating far more capacity than typical usage (over-allocation), failing to release system resources (leaked handles), and mutable default arguments that accumulate state across calls (leaking defaults).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | reuse, share or avoid creating the object | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | operate in place or pass a reference | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | make the producer lazy | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | retain only the fields that are actually used later | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | size the allocation to the actual input | yes, scales with input |
| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | manage the resource with a `with` block | **no — advisory only** |
| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | default to `None` and create the object inside the body | yes, scales with call count |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C6.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C6.S7.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C6.S1 vs C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup** — C3.S3's repair *moves* a construction out of a loop.  C6.S1's repair *reduces the number* of objects, whether or not a loop is involved.
- **C6.S3 vs C9.S2 Oversized Data Retrieval** — C6.S3 is about the shape of an in-memory sequence.  C9.S2 is about how much of an external resource is pulled in.  `f.read()` on a large file routes to both: if the repair streams from the source, it is C9.S2; if the data is already in memory and the repair only avoids a copy of it, it is C6.S3.
- **C6.S3 vs C5.S4 Unnecessary Representation Change** — C6.S3 changes an eager producer into a lazy one.  C5.S4 deletes a conversion and leaves the producer as it was.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
